title: 2025-11-20 Redwood Technical Deep Dive: Dedicated vs Hosted - Performance & Isolation
summary: SE-led technical deep dive comparing Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated deployment models for StrataAI. Discussion focused on latency/throughput tradeoffs, KV cache semantics, batching, quantization impacts, noisy neighbor risks, and VPC/on-prem networking requirements. Next steps: share benchmarks, run a 1-hour dedicated perf test, and exchange security docs.
transcript:
Header: Recorded 2025-11-20 15:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Attendees: Alicia Chen, Marcus Patel (Redwood); Javier Morales, Sana Iqbal, Liam O'Connor (StrataAI)

[00:00] Alicia (Redwood AE): Hey thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. Marcus and I will talk through the deep dive. Javier, do you want to kick off with the main performance concerns you have?

[00:12] Javier (Head of ML): Yeah hi thanks, um main points: we need p95 latency under 350ms for interactive flows, sustained throughput for batching analytics at about 200 reqs/sec with long tail seqs to 1024 tokens. Also we care about data isolation \u2014 we might need VPC or on-prem later.

[00:28] Marcus (Redwood SE): Got it. For clarification, are the 200 reqs/sec for concurrent single-request throughput or do you mean aggregated tokens per second?

[00:34] Javier: Aggregate requests, so sometimes large seq lengths, sometimes short. We have two workloads: real-time chat (short, low latency) and batch reranking (longer seqs, high throughput).

[01:10] Marcus: Okay makes sense. Quick overview: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and elastic capacity but is multitenant; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools with capacity commits, predictable throughput and guardrails against noisy neighbors. We'll focus on runtime behavior: KV cache, continuous batching, kernel selection, and quantization.

[02:05] Sana (Platform Eng): Quick Q: how deterministic is KV cache eviction on dedicated? We saw strange behavior in a PoC where prefixes were evicted under load.

[02:20] Marcus: Good question. On Redwood Dedicated we reserve GPU memory per tenant so eviction is much rarer; eviction policy still exists for extremely high concurrent sequences but it's threshold-based. In Hosted, the system is more opportunistic \u2014 prefix caching is best-effort and can be evicted when the node reclaims memory for higher priority traffic. So noisy neighbor can cause more frequent evictions in Hosted.

[02:58] Alicia: To add, Dedicated allows pinning model variants and cache sizes per pool which gives you predictable hit rates for KV cache. That maps directly to latency and cost.

[03:20] Liam (CTO): When you say \"pinning cache sizes\", is that per-GPU or per model instance? We often run multiple models on a single tenant.

[03:30] Marcus: It's configurable per-dedicated-pool and by model routing rules. For example you can reserve a dedicated pool for your rerank model with larger KV allocation and a separate low-latency pool for chat. We manage kernel selection and memory mapping per pool.

[04:05] Javier: How about continuous batching\u2014does Dedicated change how that works? We saw some variance in latencies when batch windows grew.

[04:16] Marcus: Continuous batching is runtime-level. We aim to balance latency SLOs with batching efficiency. On Hosted the runtime shares batchers across tenants, so backpressure from other tenants can increase batch size and thus latency. Dedicated gives you isolated batchers, and you can set stricter max-batch windows and latency targets in the pool policy. So you'll get more predictable p50/p95.

[05:02] Sana: Any guidance on max-batch-window values for our chat workload? We're trying to keep p95 < 350ms.

[05:12] Marcus: For short chats, we typically set max batch window at 8\u201312ms with a max-batch-size tuned to your QPS; that keeps batching latency low while still allowing modest consolidation. For heavy rerank with long seqs, larger windows are fine because throughput is the priority. We'll capture exact suggestions in the benchmark doc.

[06:00] Javier: Quantization \u2014 our models are sensitive to quality. Does Redwood support int8 vs int4 and what's the perf/quality delta?

[06:12] Marcus: Yes we support quantized execution paths. int8 gives a good perf uplift with minimal quality loss for many models; int4 is riskier but can reduce memory footprint dramatically. On-hosted we expose multiple model variants and you can fallback to a higher-precision variant if quality drops. On Dedicated you can also run quantization profiles but we recommend validating with your test prompts. Marcus (laughs): there's also per-layer kernel selection and sometimes we apply mixed precision to attention kernels to preserve quality.

[07:08] Javier: Do you do QAT (quantization-aware training) or only PTQ (post-training quant)?

[07:15] Marcus: We primarily support PTQ in the platform for quick onboarding; for customers needing QAT we work with them offline (model repo) or recommend a small QAT pipeline they run and then we deploy the resulting weights.

[07:40] Alicia: One note \u2014 int4 can affect the KV cache hit behavior because the cache entry size is smaller but precision differences change token embeddings slightly; it's another reason to A/B test.

[08:02] Liam: Noisy neighbor \u2014 what's the SLA for hosted? If multitenant events spike, do we see tail latency increase?

[08:12] Marcus: Hosted has soft isolation and traffic shaping. We have prioritization tiers; customers on paid tiers have higher priority to reduce tail effects. But because resources are shared, transient noisy neighbor issues can cause p95 spikes. Dedicated removes that by allocating GPUs to your pool with autoscaling policies you control.

[08:50] Sana: For Dedicated, what throughput guarantees can you provide? We need to know sustained tokens/sec for contract.

[09:00] Marcus: For Dedicated we provide throughput profiles\u2014these are not hard temporal SLAs like absolute tokens/sec during hardware failures, but are contractual targets tied to reserved capacity. For example a 4x A100 pool with N GPUs gives X tokens/sec for model Y at seq length Z. We include burst capacity options. We'll put exact numbers in the proposal sheet.

[09:40] Javier: Can you give a concrete example? 4 A100 GPUs, 1024 seq, what's the expected throughput for a 7B-ish model?

[09:50] Marcus: Roughly, with optimized kernels and int8 you might see Y tokens/sec\u2014(note: placeholder) \u2014but we'll run the benchmark on your actual request shapes. It's important: kernel selection, batch packing, and prefix cache behavior change numbers by 20-40% in practice.

[10:30] Alicia: We're hearing that you want a measurable benchmark \u2014 Marcus will run a dedicated benchmark with your sequences and we'll share the harness.

[10:45] Marcus: On networking: VPC/private deployments add latency for model control plane ops and for any egress. On-prem has more variance due to local network topology; we can tune colocations to minimize jitter. If you do VPC peering, we recommend colocating inference fleet in the same region as your app tier.

[11:20] Sana: What about KMS/HSM for keys? For private we need customer-managed KMS.

[11:28] Alicia: Yes private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. We'll share the security pack.

[12:00] Javier: A couple of oddities from our earlier PoC: 1) KV cache sometimes showed lower hit rates when sequence diversity was high; 2) some batch windows seemed to pack unrelated short and long seqs causing p95 to spike. Any quick counters?

[12:22] Marcus: For (1) sequence diversity reduces effective prefix reuse \u2014 we saw this. Solutions: increase cache size on Dedicated, route similar traffic to the same pool, or use prefix-keyed routing. For (2) set separate pools or routing rules so short-chat traffic doesn't get batched with long rerank jobs.

[13:05] Javier: Can routing be rule-based at request level? We have specific headers available.

[13:12] Marcus: Absolutely, routing supports headers, path, model tags. You can do header-based routing to different pools to avoid mixing.

[13:40] Liam: What visibility do we get for token-level cost and latency breakdowns?

[13:48] Alicia: Redwood Console exposes per-route token counts, cost, per-token latency breakdown and trace links. On Dedicated you also get per-pool utilization dashboards and KV cache hit rate metrics.

[14:20] Sana: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?

[14:26] Marcus: Provide sample prompts (200-500), sequence length distribution, desired quality thresholds (like acceptable BLEU/ROUGE/LLM eval metric), and a target p95. We'll generate a harness that replays traffic with appropriate QPS and seq lengths.

[15:00] Javier: We'll also need to validate failover \u2014 if a node goes down in Dedicated, how does fallback occur?

[15:12] Marcus: We support automatic fallback to other GPUs in the pool and we can configure cross-pool fallback to Hosted variants if you opt in. For Dedicated pools we also recommend a small buffer of reserved capacity to absorb failures.

[15:45] Alicia: Note on costs \u2014 Dedicated is committed cost but predictable; Hosted is variable. We can model per-token costs after the perf runs.

[16:05] Sana: Any gotchas for on-prem? Disk bandwidth, nvlink topology?

[16:14] Marcus: Yes on-prem parity requires matching NVLink mesh and PCIe lanes; kernel performance can drop if topology isn't homogeneous. We'll provide a hardware compatibility sheet.

[16:40] Javier: Can Redwood's runtime do mixed-precision attention while keeping feed-forward layers quantized?

[16:48] Marcus: Yes we do mixed precision per-kernel \u2014 attention often uses FP16 for stability while linear layers can be int8/4 depending on the profile. This is part of the kernel-selection and compilation step.

[17:22] Liam: For our compliance team: audit logs, SSO, RBAC \u2014 are those first-class on Dedicated and Private?

[17:30] Alicia: Yes, RBAC, SAML, SCIM, audit logs, and long retention options are available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted also supports enterprise SSO and audit logs but Dedicated gives you more control over retention and log export.

[18:00] Javier: Any limitations on model size for Dedicated? We might want to try a 70B model in future.

[18:10] Marcus: Larger models (50B+) require model parallelism; we support sharded execution but that changes throughput/latency calculus. For 70B we typically recommend distributed pods with NVLink and higher interconnects; we'll design specific pool shapes for that.

[19:00] Alicia: Ok let's recap next steps.

[19:07] Marcus: Action items and next steps summary: we'll run a 1-hour dedicated benchmark, share hardware/compatibility and security pack, provide a proposed pool sizing and pricing, and walk through routing rules in a follow-up.

[19:30] Javier: Sounds good. Can you also include an example of how batch windows impacted latencies in your prior benchmarks?

[19:38] Marcus: Yes we'll include P50/P95 plots and the scenario where inbound QPS variance increased average batch sizes.

[20:00] Alicia: Any final questions?

[20:05] Liam: One logistics Q \u2014 if we start Dedicated pilot, what's lead time?

[20:12] Marcus: Typical spin-up for Dedicated is 2\u20134 weeks depending on region and GPU availability; on-prem is obviously longer for procurement and colocation.

[20:30] Sana: Great thanks everyone.

[20:35] Alicia: Thanks all \u2014 we'll send the benchmark harness and security docs.

[20:40] End of recording.
